# Raxon

> A Rack 3 JSON API framework for Ruby. Routes are files, each endpoint declares
> its own OpenAPI contract next to its handler, and requests and responses are
> validated against that contract at runtime.

This file orients an agent **building an application with Raxon**. If you are
modifying the Raxon gem itself, read `CLAUDE.md` and `CONTEXT.md` instead — they
are contributor guidance and describe internals you do not need here.

A project created with `raxon new` also gets its own `AGENTS.md` covering the
same ground with that project's paths filled in.

## The rule that matters

Every endpoint declares its contract — parameters, request body, and a schema
per response status — in the same file as its handler. Responses are validated
against the declared schema at runtime, so a response with an undeclared field
fails loudly rather than silently succeeding.

**Declare the schema first, then write the handler to match.** Changing what a
handler returns without changing its declared response is the single most common
way to break a Raxon endpoint.

## A complete route file

```ruby
# routes/api/v1/users/__id__/get.rb
Raxon.route do
  description "Fetch a user by ID"

  parameters do |params|
    params.define :id, type: :uuid, in: :path, description: "User ID"
  end

  response 200, type: :object do
    property :id, type: :uuid
    property :email, type: :email
    property :created_at, type: :datetime
  end

  response 404, type: :object do
    property :error, type: :string
  end

  handler do |request, response, metadata|
    user = User.find_by(id: request.params[:id])
    next response.not_found(error: "Not found") unless user

    response.ok id: user.id, email: user.email, created_at: user.created_at
  end
end
```

## File → route mapping

The path comes from the file's location under the routes directory; the filename
is the HTTP method.

| File                                | Route                    |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| `routes/api/v1/health/get.rb`       | `GET /api/v1/health`     |
| `routes/api/v1/users/post.rb`       | `POST /api/v1/users`     |
| `routes/api/v1/users/__id__/get.rb` | `GET /api/v1/users/{id}` |
| `routes/api/v1/all.rb`              | every `/api/v1/*` request |

Valid filenames: `all`, `get`, `post`, `put`, `patch`, `delete`, `head`,
`options` (`.rb`). Anything else raises at boot with the list of valid names.
Path parameters use the dunder form `__name__`; the legacy `$name` form works
but trips on shell expansion.

An `all.rb` holds `before`/`after`/`metadata` blocks shared by everything below
it. With no `handler` it is middleware only and is not itself a route.

## The two DSL forms are equivalent

```ruby
Raxon.route do              # zero-arity: evaluated against the endpoint
  description "..."
  response(200, type: :object) { property :ok, type: :boolean }
  handler { |request, response, metadata| response.ok ok: true }
end

Raxon.route do |endpoint|   # one-arity: receives the endpoint
  endpoint.description "..."
  endpoint.response(200, type: :object) { |r| r.property :ok, type: :boolean }
  endpoint.handler { |request, response, metadata| response.ok ok: true }
end
```

Handler, before, after, and metadata blocks all receive
`(request, response, metadata)`; trailing arguments may be omitted.

## Types

`:string`, `:number`, `:integer`, `:boolean`, `:object`, `:array` (with `of:`),
`:file`, `:datetime`, `:date`, `:uuid`, `:email`, or an array of types for a
union. Omit `type:` entirely for a genuinely free-form value. A typo'd type name
raises at load with the valid list.

Constraints travel with the declaration: `required:`, `nullable:`, `enum:`,
`min_length:`/`max_length:`, `minimum:`/`maximum:`, `pattern:`,
`min_items:`/`max_items:`, and for uploads `max_size:`/`allowed_extensions:`.

## Lifecycle order

metadata (parent → child) → before (parent → child) → handler → after
(child → parent). `response.halt` stops the rest immediately. Map domain
exceptions to statuses with `config.rescue_from` rather than rescuing inside
every handler.

## Verify loop — run these after every change

```
bundle exec raxon routes                  # every route loaded, with its handler
bundle exec rake raxon:openapi:generate   # schemas compile → doc/apidoc/api.json
bundle exec rspec                         # responses conform to declared schemas
```

`raxon routes` catches bad filenames and load errors, the rake task catches
invalid schema declarations, and `conform_to_response_schema` in specs catches
handlers that have drifted from their contract. A change is not done until all
three are green.

## Scaffolding

```
bundle exec raxon new my-api
bundle exec raxon generate route api/v1/users get post
bundle exec raxon generate route api/v1/users/__id__ get
```

## Docs

- [README](README.md): full reference — routing, the OpenAPI DSL, validation, handler helpers, hooks, HTML rendering, test helpers, and every configuration option.
- [Request lifecycle](docs/lifecycle.md): exact order of metadata, before, handler, after, and where `halt` and `rescue_from` cut in.
- [Path parameters](docs/path_parameters.md): the `__name__` and `$name` directory forms, and how parameters reach `request.params`.
- [File uploads](docs/file_uploads.md): `type: :file`, the `UploadedFile` interface, and declaring `max_size` / `max_total_size` / `allowed_extensions`.
- [Security model](docs/security.md): what Raxon guarantees and what it does not — trusted route files, request size limits, ReDoS handling, upload caveats, proxy headers, and error-log safety. Read before exposing an app publicly.

## Optional

- [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md): contributor guidance for changing Raxon itself, including the OpenAPI DSL internals.
- [CONTEXT.md](CONTEXT.md): architecture vocabulary for the gem's own internals.
